claims.summary: The origin assigns liability for electioneering communications to the sponsor, not the disseminating medium, except where the medium removes a disclosure or alters content into synthetic media.
The descendant, titled "The Taylor Swift Act," defines consent, depicted individual, digital depiction, intimate digital depiction and sexually explicit conduct.
The descendant lets a depicted individual sue over nonconsensual disclosure of an intimate digital depiction, with damages, $150,000 liquidated damages, injunctions and exceptions.
The origin bars treating interactive computer services as publishers except as stated; the descendant shields them for good-faith actions restricting access to intimate depictions.
